You're investigating a git branch in the repo at /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/Zimmermann-Handover (design-to-code handover repo for client Zimmermann, component tag prefix `zimm-`). Working directory is already checked out on branch `feature/browser-preview-and-full-kit-catalog`; `main` also exists locally, up to date with origin. READ-ONLY investigation: do not edit files, do not switch branches, do not commit.

Background: the component API contract lives at 02-design/library/contract/zimm-contract.js (an array describing each component's tier, attributes, slots, and accessibility notes — treated as source of truth) and is checked by 02-design/library/contract/validate.mjs (a Node validator for atomic-model rules). The most recent commit on this branch, 6ece7d6 ("CSS dedup pass, fix broken prototypes, contract audit fixes"), claims a new audit script was written that cross-checks every component's actual attr()/bool()/slots.*/composed-tag usage in code against its contract entry, rather than trusting prior spot checks, and found + fixed 4 discrepancies:

1. zimm-navigation: contract documented one generic `menu-panel` slot; the real implementation actually has 6 (a `mobile-utility` slot plus one named `menu-*` slot per nav item).
2. zimm-text-input: a trailing slot existed in the component's code but was missing from the contract.
3. zimm-select: the contract described a permanently-floated label, but no `<label>` element is actually implemented.
4. zimm-product-detail-gallery: the contract described fixed 1200px/560px cell heights with a 4px gap; the actual implementation uses aspect-ratio sizing with no gap, and (per the commit message) always did, even before this migration branch started.

The commit also claims each fix includes a dated correction note in the contract file explaining what was wrong (not a silent rewrite), and that `validate.mjs` reports 0 violations and the audit script reports clean after the fixes.

Separately, an EARLIER commit on this same branch (d53dc39) flagged some "known follow-ups, not fixed here" — check whether these were actually resolved later or are still open in the current code:
(a) "a stale trailing-slot contract gap on zimm-text-input" — likely the same issue #2 above, check if it's now resolved.
(b) "stale sizing/label notes on product-detail-gallery and select's contract entries that don't match either the old or new implementation" — check current state.
(c) "4 undefined CSS custom properties referenced by product-detail-options that predate this migration" — this one is NOT mentioned as fixed in the later commit. Your job is to actually find these 4 (or however many currently exist) by reading 02-design/library/elements/product-detail-options/zimm-product-detail-options.css, extracting every `var(--...)` reference, and cross-checking each against every token file (common.css + 02-design/library/tokens/*.css) plus any other files where zimm- custom properties get defined, to determine whether they're genuinely undefined (dangling references with no fallback and no definition anywhere) or a false alarm.

YOUR JOB:
1. Open 02-design/library/contract/zimm-contract.js and find the actual entries for zimm-navigation, zimm-text-input, zimm-select, zimm-product-detail-gallery. Quote the relevant slot/attribute fields and any dated correction notes. Confirm each of the 4 claimed fixes is really reflected in the contract as it stands now.
2. Cross-check claim 1 (navigation) against the real implementation: read zimm-navigation.js and confirm it actually defines/uses 6 slots as described (a mobile-utility slot + one per nav item), not just that the contract says so.
3. Try running the validator for real: `cd /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/Zimmermann-Handover && node 02-design/library/contract/validate.mjs` (check the file first to confirm this is the right invocation) and report the actual output/exit code, not just the claimed "0 violations."
4. Resolve the 3 "known follow-up" items (a)/(b)/(c) above against the current contract + code state: for each, state clearly whether it is NOW RESOLVED, STILL OPEN, or PARTIALLY RESOLVED, with evidence. Item (c) is the important one — do the actual cross-check and report the specific property names if you find genuinely undefined ones, since this would be a real bug shipping in this branch.

Report back with clear verdicts per claim/item, concrete evidence (quotes, file:line, command output), under 500 words, verdicts first. Flag item (c) prominently if it's a real unresolved issue — that's the one piece of this audit most likely to still be a live bug.
